newsitem.title: USA: CBOT's Arbor to ask Board not to extend pit hours.
newsitem.headline: CBOT's Arbor to ask Board not to extend pit hours.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade chairman Patrick Arbor will ask CBOT's board on May 20 to switch course and not extend daytime pit trading hours for financial futures, according to a members' letter dated Monday.

"An in-depth review of relevant empirical data should be undertaken before we enact any decision affecting a change in our trading hours," Arbor wrote. "A decision such as this should only be made with the input and participation of members."
The board voted April 16 to extend debt futures pit trading to close one hour later at 1500 CDT/2000 GMT.
Currently, financial futures such as U.S. Treasury bond futures open pit trading at 0720 CDT/1220 GMT each day and shut daytime pit trading at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT.

Arbor said he had spoken with "numerous" exchange members and directors and also received a members' petition opposing the longer pit trading day. He noted that CBOT's Strategy Committee recommended maintaining the 1400 CDT close.
Arbor said he would also ask that financial futures traded on Project A, CBOT's after-hours electronic system, open at 1430 CDT/1930 GMT and trade overnight until 0645 CDT/1145 GMT.
Currently, financial futures on Project A trade from 1430 CDT until 1630 CDT/2130 GMT, reopen at 2200 CDT/0300 GMT and shut again at 0645 CDT/1145 GMT.
CBOT's nighttime pit trading session for debt futures currently runs from 1820 CDT/2320 GMT until 2105 CDT/0205 GMT.
The CBOT had planned to extend its daytime financial futures trading hours, eliminate nighttime pit trading and extend Project A overnight hours starting April 2, 1998.
A CBOT spokesman said CBOT members still must vote by mid-June on whether to close nightly pit trading and alter Project A hours. CBOT has not yet set a date for that vote.
